data.text: The repo has no app code yet; there is no earlier stage to wait for (ignore 'Stage 1'). Use Python 3 standard library only (http.server), in hello.py at the repo root. GET /hello returns HTTP 200, Content-Type text/plain, body exactly 'hello'. Add one unittest in test_hello.py. No other files.

decisions: Add a minimal HTTP hello endpoint using only the Python 3 standard library (http.server). Create hello.py at the repo root defining a request handler (and a way to run a server) where GET /hello responds with HTTP 200, Content-Type text/plain, and a body of exactly 'hello'. Add test_hello.py at the repo root with one unittest that starts the server (e.g. on an ephemeral port in a background thread), issues GET /hello, and asserts the status, content type, and body. No other files are added or changed; there is no prior stage to wait for (the repo currently has no app code).
Per trusted human answer: stdlib http.server only, hello.py at repo root, GET /hello -> 200 text/plain body exactly 'hello', one unittest in test_hello.py, no other files.
Server binds 127.0.0.1:8000 by default, optional port as first CLI argument.
Non-/hello paths return 404 via send_error; Content-Length: 5 is sent.
Test binds port 0 and runs the server in a daemon thread to avoid port clashes and hangs.
lessons_proposed: CI in this repo runs 'echo tests ok' and process.yaml is protected, so state in the spec that unit tests must be run by hand in UAT rather than relying on CI.

decisions: Followed plan.md exactly: stdlib http.server only; HelloHandler serves GET /hello with 200, Content-Type text/plain, Content-Length 5, body 'hello'; any other path gets send_error(404).
make_server(host, port) is exposed so the test can bind to port 0 and run the server in a daemon thread.
Test-first: test_hello failed with ImportError before hello.py existed, then passed (1 test, OK).
Smoke-checked with curl: HTTP/1.0 200 OK, Content-Type text/plain, body 'hello'; /x returned 404. The project's local CI command is 'echo tests ok'.
lessons_proposed: In this sandbox, curl to localhost goes through an HTTP proxy and returns a misleading 405. Use 'curl --noproxy "*"' for local smoke checks.

python3 -m unittest -v test_hello: 1 test, OK. Without hello.py the test fails at import, and it asserts status, Content-Type and the exact body, so it proves every required behaviour.

decisions: Reviewed hello.py and test_hello.py (the files in scope for issue #41); no git history available, so reviewed working-tree contents directly.

hello.py uses only the stdlib http.server, binds 127.0.0.1 by default, serves a fixed constant body for exact path '/hello', and returns send_error(404) otherwise; no user input is reflected, parsed, executed, or deserialized.
No secrets, credentials, crypto, third-party dependencies, file system access, or subprocess usage introduced.
No changed files fall under security.sensitive_paths or protected_paths in process.yaml.
doubts: Non-blocking: hello.py's CLI port argument is passed through int() without range checks; invalid input just raises, no security impact.
Non-blocking: http.server is documented as not for production use; acceptable for this localhost-default demo endpoint, but it should not be exposed publicly as-is.

decisions: AC1: `python3 -m unittest test_hello -v` ran 1 test in 0.5s and ended with OK.

AC2: `python3 hello.py` printed 'Serving on http://127.0.0.1:8000/hello'. `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/hello` returned 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK', 'Content-Type: text/plain', 'Content-Length: 5' and body 'hello'. `od -c` showed exactly h e l l o (5 bytes) with nothing after it.
AC3: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/other` returned 404 with the stdlib HTML error page. The body was not 'hello'.
AC4: `python3 hello.py 8081` served 'hello' at /hello. SIGINT (Ctrl+C equivalent) stopped it with exit code 0 and no traceback. The same was true of the port-8000 server.

AC5: hello.py and test_hello.py import only the standard library (http.server, sys, http.client, threading, unittest). docs/specs/41 contains plan.md, spec.md and uat.md. No requirements or dependency files exist.

curl went through the sandbox's HTTP_PROXY (concert-proxy) by default and got a fake '405 Method Not Allowed' from the proxy. I bypassed it with NO_PROXY='*' for 127.0.0.1. This is a sandbox issue, not an app issue.
doubts: AC5 was only partly checked. /work is not a git checkout (no .git), so I could not see the change's file list via git status or the PR. Other root files (.github/, live-*/pr.txt, probe-*.txt, process.yaml, README.md) look like existing repo scaffolding, but I could not confirm the change left them untouched.
lessons_proposed: The sandbox sets HTTP_PROXY, so curl to 127.0.0.1 hits the proxy and gets a fake 405. Export NO_PROXY='*' (or use curl --noproxy '*') before local HTTP checks.
In a non-interactive bash, background jobs ignore SIGINT, so `kill -INT` will not stop a Python server and `wait` hangs. Run `set -m` first so Ctrl+C can be simulated.
When killing processes by matching /proc/*/cmdline, match the exact command prefix (case "python3 app.py"*), or the loop kills its own shell.

decisions: AC1: `python3 -m unittest test_hello -v` ran 1 test (test_get_hello) and the output ended with OK.

AC2: started `python3 hello.py` (it printed 'Serving on http://127.0.0.1:8000/hello'). `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/hello` returned 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK', 'Content-Type: text/plain', 'Content-Length: 5' and body 'hello'. `curl -s ... | od -c` showed exactly 'h e l l o' (0000005), with nothing after it.
AC3: `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/other` returned 'HTTP/1.0 404 Not Found' with the default HTML error page; the body is not 'hello'.

AC4: SIGINT (the equivalent of Ctrl+C) stopped the server with exit 0 and no traceback. `python3 hello.py 8081` and then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8081/hello` printed 'hello'. SIGINT stopped it with exit 0 and no traceback.

AC5: /work is not a git checkout, so I could not run `git status` or see a PR file list. hello.py and test_hello.py import only stdlib modules (http.server, sys, http.client, threading, unittest), and there is no requirements or packaging file. docs/specs/41 contains only plan.md, spec.md and uat.md.

Environment: HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy point to concert-proxy:3128 and NO_PROXY is empty. Plain curl to 127.0.0.1 therefore went through the proxy and got '405 Method Not Allowed' from it. I set NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost for every check. No source files were changed.
doubts: AC5 was only partly checked: without git history I cannot prove that the other root files (README.md, process.yaml, probe-*.txt, live-*/pr.txt, .github/workflows/*) were unchanged by this change. They look like pre-existing repo or harness scaffolding.
lessons_proposed: The sandbox sets http_proxy with an empty NO_PROXY, so curl to 127.0.0.1 hits the proxy and gets a 405; export NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost (or use curl --noproxy '*') before local HTTP checks.

Background jobs in the harness shell ignore SIGINT, and a shell-function wrapper adds a subshell; to simulate Ctrl+C, reset SIGINT to SIG_DFL before exec and send kill -INT to the actual python PID (found via /proc/*/cmdline, because ps/pkill are not installed).

decisions: hello.py matches spec and plan exactly: stdlib http.server only, HelloHandler.do_GET returns 200, Content-Type text/plain, Content-Length 5, body b'hello'; other paths 404 via send_error; make_server defaults to 127.0.0.1:8000; optional CLI port; server closed on KeyboardInterrupt.

test_hello.py has one unittest that checks status, Content-Type and exact body against a server on an OS-assigned port, with a daemon thread, shutdown/server_close in tearDown and a 5s client timeout. Ran it: 1 test, OK. Without hello.py it fails with ImportError, so it proves the change.
Manual smoke (curl --noproxy on port 18081): HTTP/1.0 200 OK, Content-Type: text/plain, Content-Length: 5, body 'hello'; /other returns 404. AC2-AC4 in uat.md hold.
No protected paths (process.yaml, .github/**) are touched and no dependencies are added.
lessons_proposed: The sandbox routes curl through a proxy that returns 405 for localhost; use curl --noproxy '*' when smoke-testing local servers.
Without ps/pkill, do not kill by grepping /proc/*/cmdline for a pattern in the same shell command: it matches and kills your own shell. Record the PID with $! instead.

decisions: Reviewed hello.py and test_hello.py (the only app files; no git history available, so reviewed working tree). Neither touches a security.sensitive_paths or protected_paths entry.

hello.py: stdlib http.server only, no dependencies; default bind is 127.0.0.1 (not 0.0.0.0); only exact path '/hello' is served with a constant body; request path is never reflected into responses (send_error(404) uses stdlib's HTML-escaped default page); no file system access, no deserialization, no shell/eval, no secrets or credentials; default request logging to stderr contains only the request line.
Port from argv is parsed with int(), so no injection; invalid input just raises ValueError at startup.
test_hello.py binds an ephemeral port on loopback and shuts the server down in tearDown; no security impact.
doubts: Informational, not blocking: http.server is documented by Python as not suitable for production (only basic security checks, single-threaded HTTPServer can be tied up by one slow client). Fine for this scope; if this ever ships beyond local use, put it behind a real server or use ThreadingHTTPServer with timeouts.
